things_to_do: Trek the Green Route through 58 tunnels and 100+ bridges on the abandoned railway
Walk coffee plantations in peak condition
Climb to Bisle Viewpoint for 360-degree Western Ghats views
why_go: January peaks at 14–28°C with clear skies and no rain. Coffee estates are at their cleanest, and Bisle Viewpoint offers the year's sharpest views of the Western Ghats. The Green Route Trek is fully accessible.

things_to_do: Tour coffee estates during estate walks
Hike Bisle Viewpoint for panoramic views
Relax in homestays with valley vistas
why_go: February is Sakleshpur's driest month at 15–29°C. Estate walks are immaculate, Manjarabad Fort walls are clearly visible, and Bisle Viewpoint offers unobstructed 360-degree views of the Ghats.

things_to_do: Witness coffee blossoms (white carpet across estates for 7–10 days post-showers)
why_go: March opens the coffee blossom window, with white flowers carpeting estates for 7–10 days after pre-monsoon showers. Temperatures climb to 17–30°C, but mornings remain pleasant for exploration.
why_not: Late March forests lose monsoon lushness as heat builds.

things_to_do: Walk coffee estates in early mornings only
why_go: Coffee blossoms continue through the first 10 days. April heat peaks above 35°C by midday, but early-morning estate walks and fort visits remain manageable.
why_not: April heat peaks above 35°C, making afternoon trekking and outdoor exploration uncomfortable.

why_go: May brings pre-monsoon thunderstorms and humidity reaches 80%, but dawn estate walks remain viable before heat peaks. Expect greenery and occasional heavy showers.
why_not: Pre-monsoon heat and humidity make hiking uncomfortable despite the elevation.
Southwest monsoon brings 800–1000mm rainfall with Bisle landslide risk and NH-75 closures. The Green Route Trek is waterlogged and inaccessible.
Peak monsoon with 1000–1300mm rainfall makes trekking impossible and landslide risk too high. Roads remain hazardous.
Monsoon continues with aggressive leech swarms that make trekking miserable. Trails remain waterlogged and dangerous.

things_to_do: Trek the Green Route as trails reopen
Walk coffee estates in peak greenness
Hike Bisle as landslide watches ease
why_go: September marks monsoon retreat with 18–27°C and estates at their year-greenest. Bisle Viewpoint reopens, and the landscape is lush after rainfall.

things_to_do: Trek the Green Route in full season
why_go: October opens the season at 17–28°C with estates at year-greenest and coffee harvest preparation underway. Trails are fully accessible.
November at 15–28°C brings peak season with coffee harvest in full swing and Karnataka Rajyotsava (Nov 1) celebrations. Rainfall drops below 80mm.
December peaks at 14–28°C with dry skies. Coffee harvest is in its tail phase, and plantation homestays are at peak demand—book 4–6 weeks ahead.

things_to_do: Visit Ward's Lake and Don Bosco Museum
why_go: January offers cool 4–15°C skies, low tourist crowds, and clear views. Cherry blossom afterglow lingers, and Shillong's live music scene runs year-round.
why_not: Evenings grow dark by 5pm, limiting sightseeing hours in winter.

why_go: February at 5–16°C offers pre-spring conditions with clear views of surrounding hills. Tourist numbers remain low, making it a peaceful month.
why_not: Cool mornings require warm layers for dawn hikes, and fewer travellers means some services operate limited hours.

why_go: March warms to 8–20°C as spring flowers begin. The weather is pleasant, and trekking conditions are excellent.

things_to_do: Hike Shillong Peak and Elephant Falls
why_go: April at 10–22°C marks peak spring with the best weather of the season. Tourist season begins, bringing buoyant cafe culture and outdoor activities.

things_to_do: Hike early-May trails before showers intensify
why_go: May at 12–24°C remains pleasant early on, with spring flowers still visible. Pre-monsoon showers begin late month but mornings stay dry.
why_not: Late-month monsoon rains will soak most outdoor activities, so plan hiking and sightseeing for early May.
Monsoon arrives with 15–22°C and heavy rains. Waterfalls become spectacular but roads become risky, and landslides frequently close routes.
Peak monsoon with 16–22°C and very heavy rainfall. Landslide risk peaks during July's heaviest rainfall, making road travel genuinely hazardous.
Monsoon continues at 16–22°C with heavy rain. Landslides and washed-out roads make August travel unreliable despite the dramatic landscape.
Monsoon retreats slowly at 14–22°C. Roads remain waterlogged from lingering rains, limiting access to attractions.

things_to_do: Hike Shillong Peak and Elephant Falls
why_go: October at 10–22°C marks post-monsoon perfection with clear skies, green hills, and minimal rain. This is the start of the peak season.
November at 8–20°C brings the iconic Cherry Blossom Festival and clear weather. Shillong's cultural peak coincides with optimal outdoor conditions.
December at 5–18°C offers cool, clear weather and big Christmas celebrations in this predominantly Christian city. Holiday season brings festive energy.

things_to_do: Climb 614 barefoot steps to Bahubali monolith before 10am
why_go: January at 16–29°C marks peak Bahubali season. The 614-step climb is fully walkable before 10am. Vindhyagiri permits operate at full tempo.

things_to_do: Climb Vindhyagiri's 614 barefoot steps to Bahubali
why_go: February at 18–31°C is Shravanabelagola's driest month. Trail conditions are at year-best, and the 614-step climb is most comfortable.
March at 20–33°C marks the last clean window. The 614-step climb compresses to dawn hours before heat peaks.
why_not: Midday heat makes the 600+ barefoot granite steps a physical endurance test rather than a pilgrimage.

why_go: April heat peaks at 23–35°C. The barefoot climb is only viable for early starters. Humidity reaches 70%.
why_not: April heat makes the 600+ barefoot granite steps a physical endurance test rather than a pilgrimage.

why_go: May brings peak pre-monsoon heat at 23–35°C and 75% humidity. Only dawn climbing is viable.
why_not: May's peak heat makes the 600-step granite climb genuinely dangerous without early morning start.

why_go: June at 22–29°C brings monsoon arrival with 70–100mm rainfall. Dry mornings allow full Vindhyagiri climbs.
why_not: Monsoon rains make the 634 granite steps treacherously slick, multiplying accident risk for climbers.

why_go: July at 22–27°C continues monsoon with 80–110mm rainfall. Dry-morning climbs remain viable, and the hill reaches year-greenest appearance.
why_not: Monsoon rains make the 600 steps treacherous despite pleasant weather.

why_go: August at 22–28°C continues monsoon with 90–120mm rainfall. Independence Day weekend draws pilgrims. Dry mornings allow full climbing.
why_not: Monsoon rains make the barefoot Bahubali climb slippery and physically demanding.

why_go: September at 21–29°C marks monsoon retreat. Vindhyagiri climbing becomes fully reliable from week three onwards.

things_to_do: Climb Vindhyagiri's 614 steps in full season
why_go: October at 20–29°C opens the season with post-monsoon cleanliness. Vindhyagiri climbing is fully reliable and at year-best conditions.
November at 18–28°C brings high season with dry weather. The 614-step climb is at year-best. Hassan-Belur-Halebidu circuit tourism peaks.
December at 17–27°C marks peak season. The 614-step climb is at year-best with dry conditions. Christmas-NYE hotel rates climb 25%.

things_to_do: Visit Siddhivinayak temple on river island
why_go: January offers one of Siddhatek's better windows with manageable crowds and acceptable weather for the river crossing.

things_to_do: Photography of the unique right-trunk idol
why_go: February is one of Siddhatek's stronger windows with dry conditions and lower humidity for temple visits.
March remains manageable as one of Siddhatek's better-weather months for the temple visit and river crossing.
April weather and crowds are mid-range. The visit is workable but requires weather checking.

why_not: May weather and crowds make this a weaker window for temple visits.

why_go: June is a weaker window, but the monsoon-arriving landscape offers a unique appeal.

why_not: July is a weaker window with monsoon conditions limiting temple and river access.
August is a weaker monsoon window limiting access and comfort.

why_go: September weather and crowds are workable as monsoon retreat begins, making it a viable window.
October is one of Siddhatek's better windows with post-monsoon conditions and Diwali week drawing pilgrims.
November is one of Siddhatek's better windows with optimal weather for pilgrimage and temple-circuit timing.
December is one of Siddhatek's better windows with good weather for the temple visit and river crossing.

things_to_do: Trek Mukkali trail through virgin rainforest
why_go: January at 14–26°C marks Silent Valley's peak window. Mukkali permits operate at full tempo, river crossings are dry, and Lion-tailed Macaque sightings are reliable.

things_to_do: Trek Mukkali trail in driest conditions
why_go: February at 16–28°C is Silent Valley's driest month. Trail conditions are at year-firmest, and river crossings are clear.
March at 20–32°C marks heat beginning in the valley. Trails remain operational but mid-day exploration collapses after 11am.
why_not: Peak dry season leaves streams depleted and wildlife scarce during hotter hours.
Peak heat makes trails dangerous past 9am. Forest Department restricts to dawn slots only, and hiking is brutally uncomfortable.
May brings peak monsoon rains and pre-monsoon heat. Trails suspend often, making access dangerous.
Southwest monsoon closes the national park under Forest Department rule with 600–800mm rainfall.
Peak monsoon closes the park under Forest Department rule with 800–1000mm rainfall and near-zero visibility.
Monsoon continues with 700–900mm rainfall and forest closure. Onam holiday closures add to access restrictions.

why_go: September marks monsoon withdrawal at 22–27°C, but the park remains closed until October 1.
why_not: Monsoon floods make trails impassable and wildlife unpredictable despite improving weather.

things_to_do: Trek Mukkali from park reopening Oct 1
why_go: October reopens Silent Valley on Oct 1 at 20–27°C. Trails are at year-greenest with fresh monsoon growth. Permit lead extends to 5–7 days.
why_not: Post-monsoon leeches make hiking uncomfortable, and canopy visibility remains poor from lingering cloud cover.

things_to_do: Trek Mukkali trail in high season
why_go: November at 18–26°C brings high season with trail leeches gone by mid-month. Permit lead extends to 7–10 days as demand peaks.
December at 14–26°C marks peak season. Christmas-NY drives Mukkali stay bookings 21–30 days ahead. Permit lead stretches to 7–15 days.

things_to_do: Visit Tribal Museum for Warli art
Explore Dudhni Lake for water sports
why_go: January at 14–30°C marks peak Konkan-jungle window with dry skies. Mumbai weekend traffic peaks Friday afternoons.

things_to_do: Tribal Museum for Warli art exploration
why_go: February at 16–32°C is the driest stretch. Republic Day spillover thins, and resort rates hold January-peak pricing.
March at 20–34°C remains the last cool window. Holi mid-month draws crowds, but resort rates discount 20% off-Holi dates.
April at 24–36°C is pre-summer heat, but Lion Safari lions remain inactive afternoons. Resort pool and weekend plans dominate.
why_not: Peak heat makes forest trails exhausting before noon.

why_go: May at 27–39°C with 80% humidity is peak heat, but resort pools and indoor attractions remain viable.
why_not: May heat and humidity make outdoor exploration exhausting at sea level.

why_go: June at 25–32°C brings monsoon onset with 300–400mm rain. Lion Safari and Dudhni boats operate but face soggy conditions.
why_not: Monsoon flooding makes road access unpredictable in June.
Peak monsoon at 25–30°C with 500–600mm rain (annual peak) closes Lion Safari and suspends Dudhni boats.
Monsoon continues at 25–30°C with 400–500mm rain. Flooding makes roads impassable and humidity turns sightseeing miserable.

why_go: September at 24–30°C marks recovery with 200–250mm rain easing. Dudhni boats resume mid-month, and Lion Safari operations recover.
why_not: Monsoon drainage still leaving trails waterlogged through September.

why_go: October at 22–32°C opens the season with rainfall under 80mm. Diwali week drives a 5-day spike in visitation.
why_not: Occasional post-monsoon showers may interrupt outdoor plans.

why_go: November at 16–30°C brings peak season with rainfall under 30mm. Tarpa Festival draws tribal-culture enthusiasts. Weekend traffic at full strength.
December at 14–28°C marks peak season with dry skies. Tarpa Festival mid-month and Christmas-NY 50% premium—resorts sell out weeks ahead.

things_to_do: Explore Siolim House UNESCO finalist manor
why_go: January at 21–30°C marks peak Konkan winter with dry skies. Riverside village calm prevails. Heritage villas book 5–7 days ahead.

things_to_do: Visit Portuguese church and Siolim House
why_go: February at 22–31°C is the driest month. Carnival reaches Mapusa (5km), and heritage-villa scene peaks in demand.
March at 23–32°C marks the last cool window. Hotel rates slide 20%, and Holi mid-month traffic peaks briefly.
April at 25–34°C brings pre-monsoon heat with 75% humidity. River-walk and church tours collapse mid-day.
May at 26–35°C brings peak heat and 80% humidity. Pre-monsoon thunder weeks 3–4, but May 1 church novena starts.

things_to_do: Attend São João June 24 boat float festival
why_go: June 24 brings THE Siolim event of the year: a 175-year-old São João boat float festival with well-jumping, kopels (flower crowns), and feni-soaked celebrations. Southwest monsoon proper.

why_not: Peak monsoon at 24–29°C with 900–1100mm rain. Beach Goa remains unusable, boats are closed, and heavy daily rain disrupts outdoor plans.
Peak monsoon at 24–29°C with 500–700mm rain. Boat operators remain closed, and beaches across the bridge stay unsafe.

why_go: September at 24–31°C marks monsoon retreat with 250–300mm rain. Hosa and Thalassa restaurants return to full service by mid-month.

things_to_do: Visit Portuguese church and Siolim House
why_go: October at 24–31°C opens the season with 100–150mm late spillover. Coastal shacks rebuild 5km west, and hotel rates sit 30–35% below December peak.
November at 22–30°C brings peak season with rainfall under 30mm. Hosa booking 4–5 days, Thalassa 5–6 days.
December at 21–30°C marks peak season with dry skies. Christmas-NYE rates 2x. Thalassa river-deck books 7–10 days ahead.

things_to_do: Explore all 7 concentric temple enclosure walls
why_go: January at 21–30°C marks peak with Vaikunta Ekadasi tail. Paramapada Vasal closes Dec 30, 2026. Post-Ekadasi crowds surge the temple island.
February at 22–32°C is the driest month. Pagal-Ra-Pathu tail brings pilgrimage surges, and temple walks stay comfortable through afternoon.

things_to_do: Temple walks compress to early hours
why_go: March at 24–35°C marks the last cool month. Temple walks compress mid-day by late month as rates ease.
why_not: Midday heat peaks above comfort even for a 4/5 month, so start monument exploration at dawn.

why_go: April at 27–38°C brings pre-monsoon heat. Inner-prakaram walks compress to dawn hours. Hotel rates drop 30%.
why_not: Peak summer heat makes temple visits uncomfortable and exhausting.

why_go: May at 28–40°C is peak heat, but sacred pools provide relief and temple sanctums remain cool.
why_not: Extreme heat and humidity make outdoor temple exploration exhausting in May.

why_go: June at 27–37°C eases pre-monsoon heat. Trip works at reduced schedule due to monsoon rains.
why_not: Monsoon rains flood the temple grounds and surrounding areas, making navigation difficult.

why_go: July at 26–35°C eases summer. Aadi-month Tamil pilgrim density peaks. Morning walks remain workable.
why_not: Monsoon rains flood the temple grounds and make pathways impassable.

why_go: August at 25–33°C brings Aadi Perukku (Aug 3) and Aadi-Pooram. Cauvery festival days centre here, drawing Vaishnavite pilgrims.
why_not: Monsoon rains flood the temple grounds and surrounding areas in August.

why_go: September at 25–33°C marks pre-NE monsoon. Navarathri last week + early October. Pre-peak rate window.
why_not: Monsoon rains peak in September, flooding temple courtyards and restricting access to inner sanctums.

why_go: October at 23–31°C brings NE monsoon arrival. Navarathri tail + Dussehra peak. 7-prakaram walks return mid-month.
why_not: NE monsoon showers interrupt gopuram photography, though temple access stays reliable.

why_go: November at 22–30°C brings peak season with NE monsoon active. Vaikunta Ekadasi prep heats pilgrimage. Pagal Pathu opens late.

things_to_do: Vaikunta Ekadasi Dec 30: Paramapada Vasal opens
why_go: December at 17–27°C marks Vaikunta Ekadasi Dec 30, 2026—the peak of peaks. Paramapada Vasal opens. Hotel rates peak.

things_to_do: Visit Dariya Daulat Bagh palace with wall paintings
why_go: January at 17–29°C marks peak Cauvery island window with dry skies. Ranganathaswamy, Dariya Daulat, and Gumbaz all have clean access.
February at 18–31°C is the driest month with 55% humidity. Heritage walking is at year-best. Day-trips from Mysore are at full ease.
March at 20–33°C marks warming. Heritage walking compresses till 11am by month-end. This is the last clean window.
why_not: Midday heat peaks above comfort even for a 4/5 month, so start monuments at dawn.

things_to_do: Outdoor heritage walks at dawn only
why_go: April at 23–36°C brings pre-monsoon heat. Outdoor walks collapse mid-day. Hotel rates drop 30%.
why_not: April heat peaks at 40°C+, making outdoor temple exploration punishing.

why_go: May at 23–35°C brings peak heat plus pre-monsoon storms. Hotel rates hit year-low, making it affordable.
why_not: May heat peaks at 40°C+ with minimal monsoon relief yet.

why_go: June at 22–29°C brings monsoon arrival with 70–100mm rainfall. Cauvery fills. Heritage circuit works on full schedule.
why_not: Swollen Kaveri obscures temple islands and riverside pathways.

why_go: July at 22–27°C continues monsoon with 80–110mm rainfall. Cauvery at peak flow. Heritage circuit operates fully.
why_not: Swollen Kaveri makes river crossings risky and island pathways impassable.

why_go: August at 22–28°C continues monsoon with 90–120mm rainfall. Cauvery remains strong. Heritage circuit stays on schedule.
why_not: Monsoon flooding closes several temple courtyards and riverside fort paths.

things_to_do: Island temple traffic from Dasara pilgrims
why_go: September at 21–29°C brings Mysore Dasara halo. Island heritage and temple traffic surge from Dasara pilgrims visiting nearby Mysore.
October at 20–29°C marks Dasara tail + season open. Post-Vijayadashami weather is clean. Heritage circuit is at peak ease.
November at 18–28°C builds high season with dry conditions. Heritage walking is at peak. Ranganathittu birding season opens.
December at 17–27°C marks peak season with dry skies. Heritage walking is year-best. Ranganathittu birding peaks. Christmas-NYE rates climb.
